lesson.title: Angle of Tangency
lesson.module: Unit 5 Angles and Arcs in the circle (Geometry)

items.quote: Angles of Tangency
What you'll learn
items.text: The concept of the angle of tangency; How to infer the relation between the angle of tangency and the inscribed angle subtended by the same arc; The relation between the angle of tangency and the centeral angle subtended by the same arc; How to solve problems on angels of tangency.

items.quote: Angle of tangency.
Inscribed angle.
Central angle.
In the opposite figure :
items.text: In the opposite figure: $\angle ABC$ is an inscribed angle with the two sides $\overrightarrow{BA}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and arc $AC$, $\overrightarrow{BD}$ is a tangent to the circle at B. If we imagine the revolution of one of the sides of the inscribed angle, let it be $\overrightarrow{BC}$ moving away from $\overrightarrow{BA}$ so, it takes one of the positions $\overrightarrow{BC_1}$, $\overrightarrow{BC_2}$, ............

items.quote: In the opposite figure :
items.caption: Circle with centre dot; point B on the circle at the bottom; ray BA going up to A; rays from B through C, D1, D2 (all on the circle's upper right, labelled C, D1, D2) as successive positions; tangent ray BD at B pointing right with D at the end. Labels read from figure; verify.

items.quote: Does the measure of the resulted inscribed angles increase
items.text: Does the measure of the resulted inscribed angles increase such as $\angle ABC_1$ and $\angle ABC_2$, ......

items.quote: Do the mesures of m
items.text: Do the mesures of $m(\widehat{AC_1})$ and $m(\widehat{AC_2})$ increase, ......... ?

items.quote: are congruent, what do you notice ?
items.text: If $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{BD}$ are congruent, what do you notice?

items.quote: We get a larger inscribed angle in measure
items.text: Notice that: We get a larger inscribed angle in measure when $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{BD}$ are about to be congruent. $\angle ABD$ is called the angle of tangency, it is a special case of the tangent angle:

items.quote: m (∠ABD) = 1/2 m (ACD)
items.claim: The measure of angle ABD equals half the measure of arc ACD.

items.quote: The angle which is composed of the union of two
items.claim: Angle of tangency: the angle composed of the union of two rays, one a tangent to the circle and the other containing a chord of the circle passing through the point of tangency.

items.quote: The measure of the angle of tangency is
items.claim: Thus: the measure of the angle of tangency is half the measure of the arc between the two sides, i.e. m(∠ABC) = 1/2 m(arc AB).

items.quote: i.e. : m (∠ ABC) = 1/2 m (AB)
items.caption: Circle with centre dot; chord from B (bottom left of circle) to A (upper right on circle); tangent ray at B pointing right to C. Points A, B, C labelled.

items.quote: The measure of the angle of tangency is equal to the measure of
items.claim: Theorem 5: The measure of the angle of tangency is equal to the measure of the inscribed angle subtended by the same arc.

items.quote: Given : ∠ABC is an angle of tangency and, ∠D is an inscribed angle
items.text: Given: ∠ABC is an angle of tangency and ∠D is an inscribed angle. R.T.P: Prove that $m(\angle ABC)=m(\angle D)$.

items.quote: Proof : ∵ ∠ABC is an angle of tangency
items.text: Proof: ∵ ∠ABC is an angle of tangency ∴ $m(\angle ABC)=\frac{1}{2}m(\widehat{AB})$ (1). ∵ ∠D is an inscribed angle ∴ $m(\angle D)=\frac{1}{2}m(\widehat{AB})$ (2). From (1) and (2) we get: $m(\angle ABC)=m(\angle C)$. Q.E.D.
items.notes: Final line prints ∠ C instead of ∠D.

items.quote: The measure of the angle of tangency is half the measure of
items.claim: Corollary: The measure of the angle of tangency is half the measure of the central angle subtended by the same arc.

items.quote: In the opposite figure : BC is tangent to circle M, AB is a chord of tangency
items.text: In the opposite figure: ray BC is tangent to circle M, AB is a chord of tangency. ∴ $m(\angle ABC)=m(\angle D)$ (theorem). ∵ $m(\angle D)=\frac{1}{2}m(\angle AMB)$ (theorem). ∴ $m(\angle ABC)=\frac{1}{2}m(\angle AMB)$.

items.quote: ABC is a triangle inscribed in a circle, BD is a tangent
items.stem: ABC is a triangle inscribed in a circle, line BD is a tangent to the circle at B, X ∈ AB, Y ∈ BC where XY ∥ BD. Prove that: AXYC is a cyclic quadrilateral.
solution: ∵ BD is tangent to the circle at B, AB is a chord of tangency.
∵ XY ∥ DB, AB intersecting both of them
∴ $m(\angle DBA) = m(\angle BXY)$ ∴ $m(\angle BXY) = m(\angle C)$
∵ ∠BXY is exterior from the quadrilateral XYCA.

misprints.notes: Same quadrilateral named XYCA in the proof; vertex order differs (AXYC is the same cyclic quadrilateral).

items.quote: The converse of theorem 5
items.claim: Converse of theorem 5: if a ray is drawn from one end of a chord of a circle so that the angle between this ray and the chord equals in measure the inscribed angle subtended by the chord in the alternate side, then this ray is a tangent to the circle.

items.text: i.e.: If we draw ray AD from one end of the chord AB in circle M and m(∠DAB) = m(∠C) then: ray AD is a tangent to circle M.

items.quote: ABC is a triangle inscribed in a circle
items.stem: ABC is a triangle inscribed in a circle, line AD is a tangent to the circle at A, X ∈ AB, Y ∈ AC where XY ∥ BC. Prove that: line AD is a tangent to the circle passing through the points A, X and Y.
solution: Given: AD is a tangent to the circle and XY ∥ BC
R.T.P.: Prove that AD is a tangent to the circle passing through the points A, X and Y.
Proof: ∵ AD is a tangent and AB is the chord of tangency
∵ XY ∥ BC, AC intersector ∴ m(∠AYX) = m(∠C) (2)
From (1) and (2) we get: m(∠DAB) = m(∠AYX)
∴ AD is a tangent to the circle passing through the points A, X and Y.

learning_objectives.label: Calculate angles of tangency
learning_objectives.description: Calculate the measure of an angle of tangency (or an unknown arc) using the fact that it is half the measure of the arc between its sides, and equals the inscribed angle on the same arc or half the central angle.

learning_objectives.label: Prove cyclic quadrilaterals
learning_objectives.description: Prove that a quadrilateral is cyclic by using the equality of the angle of tangency with the inscribed angle together with parallel lines.

learning_objectives.label: Prove a line is tangent
learning_objectives.description: Show that a line is a tangent to a circle by applying the converse of theorem 5 (angle with the chord equals the inscribed angle in the alternate side).
